newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Patten criticises China intervention.
newsitem.headline: HK's Patten criticises China intervention.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten on Sunday criticised senior Chinese officials for interfering in matters straddling the British colony's return to Chinese rule next year.
"What has caused us rather more problems has been the need in the last few years to check so much that straddles 1997 with mainland officials," Patten said in a radio broadcast.
"We had for instance another clumsy intervention last week in the question of our port development -- an intervention based on a complete lack of understanding of our planning procedures."

Patten was responding to remarks by a senior Chinese official to the Hong Kong government earlier this week on gazetting plans to build new container terminals without first seeking Beijing's approval.

Chen Zuo'er, Chinese representative on a joint Sino-British body handling transitional matters, had attacked the plans and was reportedly adamant that China be consulted on major Hong Kong projects that straddled the 1997 handover.
China in the past has objected to other costly projects like the Chek Lap Kok airport and the Western Corridor Railway.
Hong Kong becomes a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China on July 1, 1997, with a high degree of self-rule for the next 50 years, except in matters of defence and foreign affairs.
Patten reminded Beijing that domestic issues were entirely Hong Kong's to decide after the handover.
"...the good news is that issues like that will be entirely matters for Hong Kong after next June, entirely matters for the SAR government," he said.
